title: Daily active users
task: Set result to a Series indexed by watch_date of distinct user_id count per day, sorted by date.
answer: result = streams.groupby('watch_date')['user_id'].nunique().sort_index()

title: 7-day rolling DAU
task: Set result to a Series of the 7-day rolling mean of daily active users (2 dp), sorted by date, NaNs dropped.
answer:
dau = streams.groupby('watch_date')['user_id'].nunique().sort_index()
result = dau.rolling(7).mean().dropna().round(2)

title: Cumulative minutes by month
task: Set result to a Series indexed by 'YYYY-MM' of cumulative total minutes_watched, sorted by month.
answer:
m = streams.groupby(streams['watch_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m'))['minutes_watched'].sum().sort_index()
result = m.cumsum()

title: Month-over-month minutes growth
task: Set result to a Series of month-over-month % change in total minutes_watched (1 dp), first month dropped, sorted by month.
answer:
m = streams.groupby(streams['watch_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m'))['minutes_watched'].sum().sort_index()
result = (m.pct_change() * 100).dropna().round(1)

title: Days between a user's streams
task: Set result to a DataFrame user_id, stream_id, gap_days for every stream that has a previous stream by the same user (sorted by watch_date, stream_id).
answer:
s = streams.sort_values(['user_id', 'watch_date', 'stream_id']).copy()
s['prev'] = s.groupby('user_id')['watch_date'].shift()
s['gap_days'] = (s['watch_date'] - s['prev']).dt.days
result = s.dropna(subset=['gap_days'])[['user_id', 'stream_id', 'gap_days']].astype({'gap_days': int}).reset_index(drop=True)

title: Signup cohort sizes
task: Set result to a Series of user counts per signup month ('YYYY-MM'), sorted by month.
answer: result = users['signup_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m').value_counts().sort_index()

title: Week-1 activation
task: Set result to a Series indexed by signup month ('YYYY-MM') of the % of users who streamed within 7 days of signup (1 dp), sorted by month.
hint: first stream per user, join signup, within 7 days, groupby month mean.
answer:
first = streams.groupby('user_id')['watch_date'].min().rename('first')
u = users.merge(first, on='user_id', how='left')
u['activated'] = ((u['first'] - u['signup_date']).dt.days <= 7) & u['first'].notna()
result = (u.groupby(u['signup_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m'))['activated'].mean() * 100).round(1).sort_index()

title: Monthly active retention
task: Set result to a Series indexed by 'YYYY-MM' of the number of users active in that month and the previous month, only months with a positive count, sorted.
hint: distinct (user, month) pairs; check prev month.
answer:
um = streams.assign(m=streams['watch_date'].dt.to_period('M'))[['user_id', 'm']].drop_duplicates()
pairs = set(zip(um['user_id'], um['m']))
um['ret'] = [(u, mm - 1) in pairs for u, mm in zip(um['user_id'], um['m'])]
r = um.groupby('m')['ret'].sum()
r = r[r > 0]
r.index = r.index.astype(str)
result = r.astype(int)

title: Each user's most-watched genre
task: Set result to a Series indexed by user_id giving the genre with the most minutes for that user.
hint: merge, groupby user+genre sum, idxmax per user.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
g = m.groupby(['user_id', 'genre'])['minutes_watched'].sum()
result = g.groupby(level=0).idxmax().apply(lambda t: t[1])

title: Titles = 50% of watch time
task: Set result to the number of titles (fewest, by minutes) whose cumulative minutes first reach 50% of total minutes_watched (an int).
hint: minutes per title desc, cumsum/total, count where prev<0.5.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
mt = m.groupby('title')['minutes_watched'].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
cum = mt.cumsum() / mt.sum()
result = int((cum.shift(fill_value=0) < 0.5).sum())

title: Rank titles by minutes
task: Set result to a DataFrame title, minutes, rank (dense, 1=most) for the top 5 titles by total minutes_watched, sorted by rank.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id').groupby('title')['minutes_watched'].sum().reset_index(name='minutes')
m['rank'] = m['minutes'].rank(ascending=False, method='dense').astype(int)
result = m.sort_values('minutes', ascending=False).head(5).reset_index(drop=True)

title: Share of genre minutes
context: Each title's share within its genre.
task: Set result to a DataFrame title, genre, pct_of_genre (title minutes / genre minutes * 100, 1 dp) over all streams.
hint: groupby title+genre sum, transform genre sum.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
g = m.groupby(['genre', 'title'])['minutes_watched'].sum().reset_index()
g['pct_of_genre'] = (g['minutes_watched'] / g.groupby('genre')['minutes_watched'].transform('sum') * 100).round(1)
result = g[['title', 'genre', 'pct_of_genre']]

title: Minutes wide by month
task: Set result to a pivot_table: index genre, columns watch month ('YYYY-MM'), values sum minutes_watched, fill_value 0.
hint: add a month column then pivot_table.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
m['mon'] = m['watch_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
result = m.pivot_table(index='genre', columns='mon', values='minutes_watched', aggfunc='sum', fill_value=0)

title: Longest daily watch streak
task: Set result to the maximum over users of the longest run of consecutive calendar days each with at least one stream (an int).
hint: per user distinct dates; date - rank grouping; max run.
answer:
best = 0
for uid, g in streams.groupby('user_id'):
    d = g['watch_date'].dt.normalize().drop_duplicates().sort_values().reset_index(drop=True)
    if len(d) == 0:
        continue
    grp = d - pd.to_timedelta(range(len(d)), unit='D')
    best = max(best, int(grp.value_counts().max()))
result = best

title: Churned users
context: No stream in the last 60 days before cutoff.
task: Set result to the number of users whose last watch_date is more than 60 days before 2025-07-31, among users who streamed (an int).
hint: last stream per user; compare to cutoff-60.
answer:
last = streams.groupby('user_id')['watch_date'].max()
result = int(((pd.Timestamp('2025-07-31') - last).dt.days > 60).sum())

title: MRR by month
task: Set result to a Series indexed by 'YYYY-MM' of total subscription amount per month, sorted by month.
answer: result = subscriptions.groupby(subscriptions['month'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m'))['amount'].sum().sort_index()

title: Net revenue change MoM
task: Set result to a Series of month-over-month change in MRR, first month dropped, sorted by month.
answer:
mrr = subscriptions.groupby(subscriptions['month'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m'))['amount'].sum().sort_index()
result = mrr.diff().dropna()

title: Minutes per active user by month
task: Set result to a Series indexed by 'YYYY-MM' of total minutes / distinct active users that month, rounded to 1 dp, sorted by month.
hint: two groupbys by month then divide.
answer:
g = streams.assign(mon=streams['watch_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m'))
tot = g.groupby('mon')['minutes_watched'].sum()
au = g.groupby('mon')['user_id'].nunique()
result = (tot / au).round(1).sort_index()

title: Power users
task: Set result to a Series of user_id whose total minutes_watched is in the top 10% (>= the 90th percentile).
answer:
tot = streams.groupby('user_id')['minutes_watched'].sum()
thr = tot.quantile(0.9)
result = pd.Series(tot[tot >= thr].index)

title: Minutes percentiles
task: Set result to a list of the 50th, 90th and 99th percentiles of per-user total minutes (0 dp each).
answer:
tot = streams.groupby('user_id')['minutes_watched'].sum()
result = [round(float(x), 0) for x in np.percentile(tot, [50, 90, 99])]

title: Age vs minutes
task: Set result to the Pearson correlation between user age and total minutes watched (2 dp), over users who streamed.
answer:
tot = streams.groupby('user_id')['minutes_watched'].sum().rename('mins')
m = users.merge(tot, on='user_id')
result = round(float(m['age'].corr(m['mins'])), 2)

title: Titles watched together
task: Set result to a DataFrame title_a, title_b (ids, a<b), users (distinct users who watched both), keeping pairs with 5+ users, sorted by users desc then ids.
answer:
a = streams[['user_id', 'title_id']].drop_duplicates()
p = a.merge(a, on='user_id')
p = p[p['title_id_x'] < p['title_id_y']]
g = p.groupby(['title_id_x', 'title_id_y'])['user_id'].nunique().reset_index()
g.columns = ['title_a', 'title_b', 'users']
result = g[g['users'] >= 5].sort_values(['users', 'title_a', 'title_b'], ascending=[False, True, True]).reset_index(drop=True)

title: Above personal average
context: Sessions longer than the user's mean.
task: Set result to the number of streams whose minutes_watched exceeds that user's mean minutes_watched (an int; ignore missing).
answer:
s = streams.dropna(subset=['minutes_watched'])
mean = s.groupby('user_id')['minutes_watched'].transform('mean')
result = int((s['minutes_watched'] > mean).sum())

title: Device split per plan
task: Set result to a DataFrame of stream counts with index plan and columns device (unstack of a groupby size), fill missing with 0.
answer:
m = streams.merge(users, on='user_id')
result = m.groupby(['plan', 'device']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

title: Peak viewing month per genre
task: Set result to a Series indexed by genre giving the month ('YYYY-MM') with the most minutes for that genre.
hint: groupby genre+month sum, idxmax per genre.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
m['mon'] = m['watch_date'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
g = m.groupby(['genre', 'mon'])['minutes_watched'].sum()
result = g.groupby(level=0).idxmax().apply(lambda t: t[1])

title: Completion by watch fraction bucket
task: Set result to a Series of mean completed per watch-fraction bucket, using pd.cut on (minutes_watched/runtime_min) with bins [0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.1] and labels ['0-25','25-50','50-75','75-100'] (2 dp).
hint: merge, compute frac, cut, groupby mean.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
m['frac'] = m['minutes_watched'] / m['runtime_min']
b = pd.cut(m['frac'], bins=[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.1], labels=['0-25', '25-50', '50-75', '75-100'])
result = m.groupby(b, observed=False)['completed'].mean().round(2)

title: First title each user watched
task: Set result to a DataFrame user_id, title (the title of each user's earliest stream; ties by lowest stream_id), sorted by user_id.
hint: sort by watch_date, stream_id; drop_duplicates('user_id'); merge title.
answer:
first = streams.sort_values(['watch_date', 'stream_id']).drop_duplicates('user_id')
result = first.merge(titles, on='title_id')[['user_id', 'title']].sort_values('user_id').reset_index(drop=True)

title: Genre summary
task: Set result to a DataFrame indexed by genre with streams (count), total_minutes (sum) and completion_pct (mean completed *100, 1 dp), sorted by genre.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
result = m.groupby('genre').agg(streams=('stream_id', 'count'), total_minutes=('minutes_watched', 'sum'), completion_pct=('completed', 'mean'))
result['completion_pct'] = (result['completion_pct'] * 100).round(1)
result = result.sort_index()

title: Reactivation
context: Users returning after a 30+ day gap.
task: Set result to the number of distinct users who had a gap of more than 30 days between two consecutive streams (an int).
hint: sorted gaps per user; any gap > 30.
answer:
s = streams.sort_values(['user_id', 'watch_date', 'stream_id'])
gap = (s['watch_date'] - s.groupby('user_id')['watch_date'].shift()).dt.days
result = int(s.loc[gap > 30, 'user_id'].nunique())

title: Weekly stream counts incl empty weeks
context: Reindex to a full weekly range.
task: Set result to a Series indexed by weekly period start of stream counts from 2024-01-01 to 2025-07-31, including weeks with 0 (use W-MON resample).
hint: set watch_date index, resample('W-MON').size(), reindex range.
answer:
s = streams.set_index('watch_date').sort_index()
r = s.resample('W-MON').size()
full = pd.date_range('2024-01-01', '2025-07-31', freq='W-MON')
result = r.reindex(full, fill_value=0)

title: Genre diversity per user
task: Set result to a Series of the number of distinct genres each user watched, sorted descending, top 10.
answer:
m = streams.merge(titles, on='title_id')
result = m.groupby('user_id')['genre'].nunique().sort_values(ascending=False).head(10)

title: ARPU by plan
task: Set result to a Series of average total amount per user, by plan, rounded to 0 dp.
hint: per-user total then groupby plan mean (join plan from users).
answer:
tot = subscriptions.groupby('user_id')['amount'].sum().rename('ltv')
m = users.merge(tot, on='user_id')
result = m.groupby('plan')['ltv'].mean().round()

title: 3-day rolling minutes per user (user 1)
context: Rolling on a per-user daily series.
task: Set result to a Series for user_id == 1: daily total minutes resampled by day, then a 3-day rolling sum, NaNs dropped, indexed by date.
hint: filter user 1, set date index, resample('D') sum, rolling(3).sum().
answer:
s = streams[streams['user_id'] == 1].set_index('watch_date').sort_index()
d = s['minutes_watched'].resample('D').sum()
result = d.rolling(3).sum().dropna()
